The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
worked_solution:
The graph consists of two parts: the line segment for $x\in [-3,0]$ and the line segment for $x\in (0,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,0].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 3 \\  & =4.5.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,4].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =ab \\  & =2\cdot 4 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-8.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4.5-8 \\  & =-3.5.\end{aligned}
$$
